## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Samuddavāṇijajātaka* (Ja 466), translated into English as *The Sea-Merchants*, belongs to the Pali Jātaka collection. According to the traditional framing narrative, the Buddha delivered the story while residing at Jetavana concerning Devadatta, after the latter had fallen into hell taking five hundred families with him [Fausböll 1887]. The opening verse of the text begins with the words *Kasanti vapanti te janā* [Fausböll 1887].

Charles Eliot highlights the story as evidence that maritime voyages and large-scale maritime migrations were familiar themes in ancient Indian society [Eliot 1921]. A verse from this Jātaka also finds a corresponding form in the Prakrit Dhammapada [Barua 1921].

In terms of text reuse and parallels, DharmaNexus detects 14 matching segments between the canonical verses and the fourth volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-linguistic alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Jātakamālā* (D4150, with 21 matches) and minor matching segments with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) [DharmaNexus].
